claims.statement: The Python reference implements the tested hak.canonical-json.v1 strict subset, enforces the machine-readable profile contract, reproduces the shared positive golden bytes/digests, and rejects the shared negative corpus.

The dependency-free Rust lane independently enforces the same machine-readable profile values and exact object shape, reproduces the shared golden canonical bytes and profile-bound SHA-256 digests, and rejects the shared negative corpus.

For the committed HAK v1 golden corpus, Python and Rust agree on canonical UTF-8 bytes and profile-bound SHA-256 digests, including UTF-16 key ordering and preservation of distinct Unicode normalization forms.

required_checks.description: Resolve, checkout, and assert the exact PR head.
Compile the HAK-015 Python reference and validate machine-readable profile/vector JSON syntax.
Run the Python reference against the exact machine-readable profile and shared positive/negative golden corpus.
Compile the dependency-free Rust reference plus exact-shape profile validator and run both against the same machine-readable profile and shared golden corpus.
Lint the HAK-015 machine-readable qualification plan.
Lint the HAK-015 HAK-010 precommitted obligation-to-step binding policy.

required_negative_cases: UTF-16 key ordering replaced by code-point ordering
canonical profile omitted from digest preimage
Rust exact-shape profile validator accepts unknown profile field

independence.claim_interpretation: limited to HAK-015 canonical evidence encoding, machine-readable profile enforcement, and tested cross-runtime golden-vector portability; does not establish semantic truth, provider authenticity, or runtime authority
